Alright, let's imagine for a moment that I'm a dad at home, trying to have a conversation with my 6-year-old who seems to have a knack for interruptions. It can indeed be quite challenging!

Now, if we shift back to psychology, this situation is actually a great example of operant conditioning. Every time I say 'dada,' my child is reinforced (attention) for interrupting, which may unintentionally encourage them to do it more often.

To address this, I might try to ignore the interruptions and wait for a pause in the interrupting behavior before responding. This is known as the "ignore" technique, which can help reduce the frequency of the unwanted behavior over time. It's important to remember to praise the child when they are not interrupting, too, to reinforce the behavior we want to see.
